name: Memoir
hint: A chapter of a life around one question: the then-self lives through it, the now-self understands what it meant.

parts.title: Before
chapters: The moment
(ca 0-2 %) Open with a scene that carries the book's question, ideally from its most charged moment, and explain nothing yet.
The question
(ca 5 %) Let the now-self step forward briefly: what you are trying to understand, and why you are writing it now.
Life before
(ca 10-20 %) The place, the people and what the then-self believed and wanted, in concrete scenes rather than background.
The first sign
(ca 22 %) A small event that pointed ahead in hindsight, written as the then-self lived it.

parts.title: What happened
chapters: The turning point
(ca 30 %) The event that splits life into before and after, as a full scene with senses and dialogue.
New rules
(ca 40 %) How everyday life changed: summarise the weeks, but stay in scene wherever something is at stake.
The people around you
(ca 50 %) Those who helped, betrayed or simply stayed, each shown through something they did.
What you didn't say
(ca 60 %) What you hid from others or from yourself, and what it began to cost.

parts.title: The reckoning
chapters: The hardest part
(ca 70 %) The lowest point, written without sparing yourself and without the now-self offering comfort.
The truth
(ca 80 %) A conversation, a letter or a discovery that makes it impossible to go on as before.
The choice
(ca 85 %) What you did, and how the then-self understood it in the moment, before hindsight.

parts.title: What it meant
chapters: Afterwards
(ca 90 %) The consequences, as honest about what went wrong as about what went right.
Understanding
(ca 94 %) The now-self looks back: what you see today that you couldn't see then, and what is still unresolved.
Back to the moment
(ca 98 %) Return to the opening scene or place and show what has changed in you.

name: Non-fiction
hint: For the explanatory and practical book: the reader's problem, a clear promise and one idea per chapter, with evidence and examples.

parts.title: The promise
chapters: The reader's problem
(ca 3 %) Open with a concrete situation in which the reader recognises their own problem.
The promise
(ca 6 %) Say what the reader will be able to do, know or understand after the book, and how the book will get them there.
Why it's hard
(ca 10 %) Show why the usual answers fall short. This is where you earn the reader's trust.

parts.title: The foundation
chapters: What you need to know first
(ca 18 %) The concepts and facts the rest of the book rests on, and nothing more.
The first idea
(ca 30 %) One claim stated plainly, with evidence, an example and what it means for the reader.
The second idea
(ca 42 %) The next claim, built on the first. Show the link in the very first paragraph.
A case in depth
(ca 52 %) A case, a person or an experiment that shows the ideas at work in real life, from start to finish.

parts.title: Going deeper
chapters: The third idea
(ca 62 %) The most surprising or difficult idea, now that the reader has the footing to take it in.
The case against
(ca 72 %) The counterarguments and where knowledge runs out. Honesty here makes the rest of the book stronger.
Common mistakes
(ca 80 %) How it usually goes wrong, and how readers can spot the signs in themselves.

parts.title: Putting it to use
chapters: How to do it
(ca 88 %) Concrete steps in order that the reader can take tomorrow, or in an explanatory book: what the reader now sees differently.
When it doesn't go to plan
(ca 94 %) The most common obstacles along the way, and what the reader does then.
Conclusion
(ca 98 %) Tie back to the promise from the start: the essentials in brief, and the way forward.
